newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares rise 1.61 pct in lower volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares rise 1.61 pct in lower volume.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose 1.61 percent in late buying as investors remained inactive after a four-day holiday, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed 25 points up at 1,578. Trade volume was lower at 24.4 trillion lira against Friday's 31.86 trillion.
Turkish markets were closed on Monday and Tuesday for a Moslem holiday.
Brokers said the rise in the afternoon session emerged amid some selective activity, led by the banking sector shares.
"The demand in Isbank C shares pulled the financial index up. Energy sector shares also helped the index rise," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank securities.
Despite the rise, brokers said the index would continue to stay in a tight range between 1,530-1,600 during the rest of the week.

The index fell 3.24 percent last week, adding the losses to 8.65 percent since January 27 when it hit its all-time high closing of 1,700. It had surged 74.2 percent from end-1996 to January 27 in a strong uptrend.

Of the 237 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 111 to 83 and 43 closed unchanged. The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN rose 1.18 percent to 1,632, the IMKB Services .XUHIZ edged down 0.14 percent to 1,458 and the IMKB Financial .XUMAL jumped 3.04 percent to 1,591.
Top actives were Isbank's C series shares, up 5,000 lira at 39,500, and largely stated-owned iron and steel maker Erdemir which rose 250 lira to 21,750.
